title: Can Multimodal LLMs ‘See’ Science Instruction? Benchmarking Pedagogical Reasoning in K–12 Classroom Videos
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether current large language models and multimodal large language models can reliably analyze K–12 science classroom instruction from video, not just from transcripts. The authors argue that science classrooms pose a harder test than mathematics because important instructional meaning is often distributed across speech, gestures, student actions, drawings, whiteboards, and other artifacts that transcripts alone miss. To study this, they introduce SciIBI, a benchmark for Core Instructional Practice (CIP) coding in science instruction, and evaluate eight state-of-the-art LLMs/MLLMs under zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting.

The benchmark contains 113 NGSS-aligned classroom clips sourced from YouTube, spanning elementary through high school science lessons, with expert consensus annotations for four CIP categories and within-practice sophistication levels. Models were evaluated on transcript-only input and on video-plus-transcript input, and they were also required to provide supporting evidence for their predictions. The study finds that all models perform modestly at best, with the strongest result reaching 53.6% accuracy, far below prior performance on math discourse benchmarks. Visual input sometimes improves performance, especially when classroom artifacts are essential, but gains are inconsistent across models and practices.

A major contribution of the paper is its evidence-based error analysis. The authors show that models often rely on surface cues such as question forms or explanation-related keywords rather than genuine pedagogical reasoning, and that good classification accuracy does not always correspond to good evidence quality. They conclude that science classroom discourse analysis remains a challenging frontier for multimodal AI and suggest an evidence-first human-AI workflow in which models retrieve candidate evidence to support expert review rather than replacing human coders.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed benchmark/evaluation study with a clear methodology, expert consensus annotation, controlled prompting comparisons, and human-rated evidence quality assessment. However, it is not an RCT or QED of a student intervention; it is primarily diagnostic/benchmarking research rather than causal impact evaluation.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper shows modest, mixed gains from visual context for model performance (+4.8 pp average across MLLMs; best +7.1 pp), but no direct educational outcome improvement for students or teachers was measured. Its practical impact is suggestive but remains limited to model benchmarking and proposed workflow support.

interventions.use_case: Benchmarking and evaluating multimodal LLMs for automated coding of K-12 science classroom video clips into Core Instructional Practices, including transcript-only vs vision+text prompting and evidence-based justification of predictions.

finding.finding_summary: This benchmark study finds that current LLMs/MLLMs show limited and inconsistent performance on science classroom pedagogical reasoning. Across eight models, zero-shot accuracy ranged from 39.1% to 53.6% on 113 clips, with the best result coming from InternVL3-78B using vision+text (53.6%, +7.1 pp over text-only), but many errors reflected surface-level shortcut use rather than genuine pedagogical understanding.
finding.measure: Accuracy and macro-F1 on 4-way Core Instructional Practice (CIP) classification; within-practice sophistication accuracy; Evidence Quality Score (EQS) ratings

finding.finding_summary: The paper does not test end-user learning gains, but it explicitly evaluates whether MLLMs could accelerate expert review of classroom video by retrieving evidence spans for human verification. The authors argue the strongest near-term utility is as an evidence-first retrieval assistant, potentially reducing the time and labor required for expert CIP coding, though no direct workload reduction was measured.
finding.measure: Evidence-based coding support / expert review assistance concept; no direct workload metric reported
finding.study_size: n=60 model outputs rated for EQS; n=113 clips total
